subject: Post-demo: FinX PII logging samples & export format
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Tom Baker <tom.baker@finxpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: FinX PII logging samples & export format

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciated the candid run-through of FinX's ingestion flow and compliance constraints. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we have the same next steps: 

1) Logs / evidence you want to review
- "who/when" access extracts for API and Console: event, actor, resource, action, timestamp, source IP, region.
- A sample of exported rows for a 7-day window (we'll sanitize values on our side if needed).

2) Preferred export formats
- We typically provide CSV or Parquet; if you need syslog/JSON-lines let us know. I attached a small CSV with the column names we usually output (requested_log_fields.csv).

3) Data residency / redaction requirements
- You mentioned that any exported logs must not include raw PAN or unredacted SSNs. Can you confirm the fields we should mask or redact before export, or if you'd prefer Redwood to perform the redaction step?

4) Timeline / gating
- If you can send the compliance checklist or a prioritized list of artifacts by EOD Friday Nov 6, we can scope a sample export and share within 48 hours for your audit team.

Attachments: requested_log_fields.csv (headers only), sample_query_script.sql (example of a time-bounded extract).

Next steps I propose: you confirm the redaction approach and preferred export format; we deliver a 7-day sample extract with column headings and a short README on how we generated it.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Tom Baker <tom.baker@finxpay.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@finxpay.com>, security@finxpay.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 17:30:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FinX PII logging samples & export format

Appreciate the follow-up, Rachel — great demo.

A few clarifications from our side:
- Confirming we need a who/when for both user-facing Console actions and machine/service API keys.
- For the sample, please remove any raw PAN/SSN columns before sending. Masking with tokenized IDs (e.g., token_XXXX) is fine.
- CSV is our preferred review format for now; Parquet is also acceptable if you can include a small README.

I'm attaching an internal doc with our compliance asks (FinX_Compliance_Reqs_v2.pdf). The key items relevant to the export:
- Retention window we want to validate against: 24 months for event-level logs.
- Export schema should include request_id and correlation_id when available.

We can share a secure S3 bucket or an internal transfer method — security@finxpay.com is looped to advise on preferred ingestion (S3 presigned vs. encrypted transfer).

Would like the sample by Monday Nov 9 to present to the internal audit team that week. Let me know if that timeline works.

Thanks,
Tom Baker
Head of Partnerships
FinX Payments
Tom.Baker@finxpay.com | +1 (212) 555-6410

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Tom Baker <tom.baker@finxpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:10:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FinX PII logging samples & export format

Thanks Tom — that works. Quick answers inline and next ask: 

- Who/when scope: we'll include Console UI events + API key events. We'll add request_id and correlation_id columns where present.
- Redaction: Redwood can perform tokenization before export (preferred) — unless you require traces of original values for internal matching. If you want us to token-match, we'll need a short table describing which columns are allowed to be tokenized vs. omitted.
- Retention verification: we can include a metadata manifest showing the event timestamp range and the retention class (hot/warm/archived) for the sample.

Plan & timeline: 
- Today (Fri) — we confirm redaction approach (please reply to this thread with which columns to redact vs. token-match).
- Mon 9 Nov — provide a 7-day sample CSV with README and a small SQL script showing the extraction query (sample_query_script.sql).

Suggested transfer: presigned S3 with AES256 server-side encryption (we can generate one-time URLs). If FinX prefers a specific bucket, send the bucket ARN and an upload path.

Forwarding your compliance doc to Neha to confirm the manifest fields we'd include for audit purposes.

Best,
Rachel

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FinX PII logging samples & export format

Looping in our security checklist items — thanks for the detail, Tom. A couple of quick notes from the security review side: 

- Tokenization performed by Redwood before export is acceptable provided the tokenization scheme is non-reversible and documented. We'll include a short tokenization appendix in the README.
- Please confirm whether IP addresses need to be truncated to /24 before export for EU users (if any). If FinX requests per-country redaction rules, flag that now.
- We'll generate the sample as CSV with a manifest.json (metadata) — if you prefer no JSON file, we can bake the metadata into a README.txt instead.

Rachel — I can take lead on producing the manifest and the README. Tom — please confirm the preferred S3 transfer method and the list of columns to redact by EOD Friday.

-Neha

Redwood Inference
